news.title: Spanish World Cup-winner Jenni Hermoso leaves Mexican club Tigres
news.lede: The 36-year-old forward, who has played 125 times for Spain, joined Tigres in 2024, having spent 18 months with another Mexican club, Pachuca. Prior to that, she played for Atletico Madrid, Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain. "I’m leaving Tigres very happy with everything I’ve experienced, but also sad, of course, because I don’t like saying goodbye, while knowing full well that this is the best thing that has ever happened to me in life," a tearful Hermoso said in a video posted on X. Her departure comes three years after the Luis Rubiales affair, which deeply affected her career and Spanish football.

news.title: New Zealand Football withdraws support for Infantino, urges review
news.lede: New Zealand Football said on Friday it had withdrawn support for FIFA boss Gianni Infantino and called for an independent review into his aborted plan to sell off part of the World Cup. Infantino came under renewed fire this week in an open letter signed by three confederations -- UEFA, North and Central America's CONCACAF and Asia's AFC -- accusing the world football boss of breaking trust "through deception". It is believed they want the Swiss official to resign before he has the chance to seek re-election in March next year. New Zealand Football became the latest FIFA member to withdraw support on Friday.

news.title: It's a middle-class sport now: Rising costs are forcing migrant kids out of football
news.lede: During the four years that he spent working as the sporting director as Hearts, Joe Savage encountered numerous children from refugee, asylum seeker and ethnic minority communities who had aspirations to become professional footballers one day. Savage, who has also worked in talent identification and recruitment with Hamilton Academical in Scotland and Norwich City and Preston North End in England, was invariably impressed with their mentality and ability when he did so. “Kids who have come over to this country with their families and had ambitions to play the game for a living have always got great attitudes in my experience,” he said. “They want to adapt, they want to do the very best they can.

news.title: FIFA crisis timeline: From World Cup final to global standoff
news.lede: HERE is a timeline of events where FIFA president Gianni Infantino introduced a proposal to sell a slice of the World Cup's commercial future that backfired and sparked a global revolt in the sport:. July 19 - The first 48-team World Cup concludes at New York New Jersey stadium with Infantino and U.S. President Donald Trump, booed as they walked onto the pitch, presenting the trophy to Spain after their 1-0 win over Argentina. July 28 - Shortly after a leak in the British media, FIFA announces it wants to create a US$20 billion subsidiary to run the World Cup and other competitions, raising US$4.2 billion for soccer development by selling a 20% stake to external investors.

news.title: WAFCON Exit, World Cup Miss: Has Nigeria Lost It Completely?
news.lede: This may not be the best period in Nigerian football as the Super Falcons, unarguably one of the most decorated national teams in the world, set two records, albeit negatively, in less than seven days. For the first time since the inception of the Women Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON), the serial winners, Super Falcons of Nigeria, failed to reach the semifinal. Similarly, the ten times African champions, for the first time since the start of the FIFA Women World Cup in China in 1991, failed to qualify for the quadrennial competition, all these happening at the ongoing WAFCON in Morocco where the team was billed to defend its title, having won the competition for the record tenth time two years ago in the same Morocco.

news.title: From football legacy to basketball: Al Janoub Arena opens with Qatar-China clash on 27th
news.lede: The Al Janoub Stadium will enter a new chapter when on August 27 the iconic venue will officially open its doors to basketball hosting Qatar’s clash with China in the fourth window of the Asian qualifiers for the FIBA Basketball World Cup Qatar 2027. More than a competitive fixture, the game will provide an early test of readiness and offer fans a glimpse of the World Cup experience, exactly one year before the global tournament begins.2022 to 2027: Qatar’s sporting legacy moves forward The FIBA Basketball World Cup Qatar 2027 will stand apart as a landmark edition in the history of the competition. It will be the first World Cup hosted by an Arab country and the Middle East and North Africa region, and the first to be staged entirely within a single city, Doha. For fans, this unique format will create the opportunity to attend more than one game in a single day.
